## Create the chart

This example uses fictional data and Plotly's graph objects, so pandas is not
required. Install `jupyter` and `plotly` before rendering.

```{python}
#| label: prepare-interactive-data
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import HTML, display

months = ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun"]
regions = {
    "North": [120, 135, 128, 160, 175, 190],
    "South": [95, 110, 115, 125, 140, 155],
}
fig = go.Figure()
for region, sales in regions.items():
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=months, y=sales, name=region, mode="lines+markers",
        hovertemplate="%{x}: %{y} units<extra>%{fullData.name}</extra>",
    ))

fig.update_layout(
    title="Fictional monthly sales by region",
    xaxis_title="Month", yaxis_title="Units sold",
    template="plotly_white", hovermode="x unified",
    margin=dict(t=110),
    updatemenus=[dict(
        buttons=[
            dict(label="All regions", method="update", args=[{"visible": [True, True]}]),
            dict(label="North", method="update", args=[{"visible": [True, False]}]),
            dict(label="South", method="update", args=[{"visible": [False, True]}]),
        ],
        direction="down", x=0, y=1.2,
    )],
)
```

```{python}
#| label: show-interactive-chart
# Embed Plotly locally in the HTML instead of fetching it from a CDN.
display(HTML(fig.to_html(
    full_html=False, include_plotlyjs=True,
    config={"responsive": True, "displaylogo": False},
    default_height="480px",
)))
```

## Try the interactions

- Hover over a point to see its value.
- Use the dropdown to show one region or both.
- Click a legend entry to hide or show that region.
- Drag over the chart to zoom, then double-click to reset.

The table provides the same values without requiring chart interaction.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print("| Month | North | South |")
print("|:------|------:|------:|")
for month, north, south in zip(months, regions["North"], regions["South"]):
    print(f"| {month} | {north} | {south} |")
```

The exported HTML includes the data and chart library and needs no Python server
to interact with it. This example targets HTML; PDF and Word do not preserve
these interactions.
